summary: This continuation reconstructs overconvergent F-isocrystals from their extremal slope data. It develops bounded quotients, PBQ filtrations and saturation over local analytic fields and curves, connects these to dagger hulls and the minimal slope property, and uses Lefschetz curves over finite fields. It separates existence of an isomorphism from lifting a prescribed quotient map and records the precise inputs each assertion needs.

nodes.title: Generic bounded solutions
nodes.statement: For a finite (φ,∇)-module M/E, pull back through τ:E→E[[u]]₀, τ(a)=Σ ∂^i(a)u^i/i!. Define Solη(M)=Hom∇(τ*M,E{u}), with E{u} the analytic functions on the open unit disc, and Solη,0(M)=Hom∇(τ*M,E[[u]]₀). These are E-vector spaces with induced semilinear Frobenius; the bounded space uses a uniform coefficient bound, not pointwise convergence. The same construction applies to B∈{E_η, E_α} of MS.0/curve-generic-field, at the generic point t_* of B^τ.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: Import the Taylor map and generic-disc solvability from RD.1. Use the contravariant horizontal Hom and induced Frobenius.
Bounded-disc multiplication preserves uniformly bounded coefficients, hence defines the bounded E-subspace.
acceptance: For the trivial rank-one connection, both solution spaces have dimension one.
Both spaces of the zero module are zero.
The solvable rank-two connection with a horizontal coordinate log(1+u)=Σ_{n≥1}(−1)^{n+1}u^n/n has an unbounded solution: at n=p^r its coefficient norm is p^r.

nodes.title: Completed generic and local fields of a curve
nodes.statement: Let C be a smooth connected affine curve over k with smooth completion C̄, a smooth affine lift Spec A_C over O_K whose weak completion carries a q-Frobenius lift φ over σ, and a generically étale coordinate x. The completed generic field E_η is the p-adic completion of the localisation of A_C at the prime πA_C, with π inverted: a complete discretely valued field with the value group of K and residue field k(C), to which φ and d/dx extend uniquely. For a closed point α of C̄, with K_α the unramified extension of K with residue field k(α) and x_α a lifted local coordinate, E_α, E†_α and K_α[[x_α]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers in x_α over K_α, and there are injective maps compatible with φ and the derivation: E_η→E_α, Â_{C,K}→K_α[[x_α]]₀ for α∈C, and A†_{C,K}→E†_α for α∈C̄∖C. For a (φ,∇)-module M† over A†_{C,K} put M_η=E_η⊗M†, M_{0,α}=K_α[[x_α]]₀⊗M† and M†_α=E†_α⊗M†. With B∈{E_η, E_α}, the generic disc of B uses the Taylor map f↦Σ_n (d^nf/dx_*^n)(t_*)(X−t_*)^n/n! into B^τ[[X−t_*]]₀.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
C is a smooth connected affine curve over the perfect field k with a smooth lift admitting a Frobenius lift compatible with σ; such lifts exist by the parent's Monsky–Washnitzer theory.
proofSteps: The special fibre of Spec A_C is integral, so the localisation of A_C at πA_C is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π and residue field k(C); complete p-adically and invert π (Tsuzuki §3.1, p.11). This is the parent Cohen-type carrier Γ^ℓ[π^{-1}] for the trivially valued field ℓ=k(C).
φ preserves πA_C and extends by continuity; d/dx extends because dx generates Ω¹ at the generic point, x being generically étale.

For a closed point α the completion of A_C along α with the coordinate x_α gives K_α[[x_α]]₀; at boundary points the overconvergent sections map to E†_α. Frobenius and derivation extend uniquely and compatibly to all rings of the two diagrams in Tsuzuki §3.1, p.11.
Independence of the lift, coordinate and Frobenius lift for solvability and boundedness is Tsuzuki Proposition 3.6, p.14, through the parent Taylor comparison.
acceptance: The generic field of the affine line has residue field k(x), not the Laurent field k((x)).
The generic module of the unit object is E_η with the trivial connection.
The gap series Σ_{n≥0}x^{n!} lies in the Amice field E_0 at the origin but not in E_η.

nodes.title: Maximally bounded quotient
nodes.statement: A (φ,∇)-module over E is bounded when its Taylor realisation is trivial over E[[u]]₀. Let Mᵇ be the unique least differential submodule whose quotient is bounded. Equivalently M/Mᵇ is the universal bounded quotient; Mᵇ is the common annihilator of Solη,0(M) under evaluation. Write B(M)=M/Mᵇ; zero has B(0)=0. The same definition applies over the completed generic field E_η of a curve and over E_α (MS.0/curve-generic-field), as in Tsuzuki §§3.3–3.6.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: Use the Taylor solution pairing and finite-dimensionality. Intersections of two kernels with bounded quotients again give a bounded quotient by embedding in their direct sum.
Choose a kernel of minimal dimension; finite intersection makes it contained in every other such kernel. Frobenius transports the universal property, so Mᵇ is Frobenius stable.
acceptance: 0ᵇ=0 and B(0)=0; no nonzero quotient is asserted for M=0.
B(B(M))=B(M), whereas the kernel convention gives B(M)ᵇ=0.

nodes.title: Bounded splitting theorem
nodes.statement: Over E (the Amice field over K, or over K_α) with perfect coefficient residue k, and over the completed generic field E_η of a curve, M is bounded iff its increasing slope filtration splits as a direct sum of pure differential Frobenius modules. In particular every pure object is bounded; for nonzero M its maximal pure slope quotient is nonzero and bounded.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: For a pure module use a Frobenius-stable unit-root lattice after an allowed slope twist and the generic Taylor estimates (Ohkubo Proposition 5.9, p.26).
For bounded M apply bounded-extension-splitting to successive pure slope grades, normalising the smallest slope first. The off-diagonal analytic cases, including gap one, are essential.
Descend the unique distinct-slope splittings and induct through the filtration. This proves differential splitting, rather than just a splitting after forgetting the connection.

For B=E_η (Tsuzuki Theorem 3.10, p.14): take the unique upper-triangular solution X over the completed perfection Ê^perf_η of A·φ(X)=X·diag(A_11,…,A_rr) for the Frobenius matrix A in a slope-adapted basis. By the local case at a closed point α, X has entries in E_α; Lemma 3.11 gives E_η=Ê^perf_η∩E_α inside Ẽ_α (from k(C)=k(C)^perf∩k(C)_α, the p-th powers being the kernel of a derivation), so X has entries in E_η.
acceptance: A nontrivial extension between distinct slopes need not be bounded merely because it is solvable.

sources.match: Theorem 3.10 states that a φ-∇-module over B∈{E_η, E_α} is bounded exactly when it is the direct sum of its slope graded pieces; the local case is CT11 Theorem 4.1, and the generic case descends the upper-triangular splitting matrix through Lemma 3.11, E_η=Ê^perf_η∩E_α inside Ẽ_α.

Theorem 4.1 (k perfect) proves that a φ-∇-module over the Amice field is bounded if and only if it is the direct sum of its pure slope pieces, deducing it from Proposition 4.2 and boundedness of pure objects.
Proposition 5.9 records that a pure (φ,∇)-module over E is bounded (its printed equality is corrected in E31); Theorem 8.3 restates the CT11 splitting theorem.

nodes.title: Pure bounded quotient
nodes.statement: A nonzero (φ,∇)-module M/E is PBQ if B(M) is pure of a single Frobenius slope. For a module over K[[t]]₀ or E†, PBQ means PBQ after scalar extension to E. The zero object is excluded from this predicate, following Tsuzuki (Ohkubo Definition 5.10 instead counts zero as PBQ), but is allowed as the initial filtration term. The definition applies verbatim over E_η and E_α.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: Form the bounded quotient and use the parent notion of a pure Frobenius module.
Nonzero M has a nonzero bounded maximal-slope quotient; bounded splitting identifies the slope of B(M) with λmax(M) when B(M) is pure.
acceptance: Every rank-one differential Frobenius module is PBQ.
Zero is not PBQ.
The split sum of two rank-one constant objects of distinct slopes is bounded but not PBQ.

nodes.title: PBQ quotient criterion
nodes.statement: For nonzero M/E the following are equivalent: M is PBQ; every nonzero differential Frobenius quotient Q of M has λmax(Q)=λmax(M). A sum of finitely many PBQ subobjects of the same maximal slope is PBQ; every nonzero quotient of a PBQ object is PBQ of that same maximal slope. The same holds over E_η, using the E_η case of bounded-splitting.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: Use bounded splitting to produce a pure lower-slope quotient if B(M) has more than one slope.
If a quotient has smaller maximal slope, quotient M by its lower slope terms and split the slope-separated extension to obtain a bounded quotient with two slopes.
Apply the criterion to sums and quotients.

Proposition 8.1 proves that PBQ implies every nonzero quotient keeps the maximal slope, and the converse when k is perfect via the splitting theorem; Lemma 8.2 supplies the splitting of slope-separated extensions.

Tensoring a Frobenius module with nonzero slope-zero U preserves and reflects purity and the maximal slope.

nodes.title: Bounded base change
nodes.statement: Let B⊂B′ be an extension of complete discretely valued fields with compatible Frobenius lifts and derivations sharing a coordinate x, for instance a finite isometric coefficient extension E⊂E_L, the generic-to-local embedding E_η⊂E_α (with x=x_α), or the finite unramified extension E_η⊂E_{η′} induced by a finite étale cover of curves. For a solvable (φ,∇)-module M over B, Sol and Sol₀ of B′⊗M are the B′^τ-spans of those of M; consequently (B′⊗M)ᵇ=B′⊗Mᵇ and B(B′⊗M)=B′⊗B(M).
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: Taylor solutions of B′⊗M are B′^τ-combinations of those of M, since the generic solution matrix of M is a fundamental solution over B′^τ as well (Tsuzuki Proposition 3.14, p.15, and its displayed identifications).

If a B′^τ-combination Σc_if_i of solutions is bounded, choose a basis d_1,…,d_m of the B^τ-span of the c_i; a finite-dimensional B^τ-subspace of the complete field B′^τ carries the product topology, so boundedness of Σd_jg_j forces every g_j to be bounded. Hence bounded solutions of B′⊗M are spanned by bounded solutions of M.

Take annihilators under the evaluation pairing to obtain (B′⊗M)ᵇ=B′⊗Mᵇ (Corollary 3.15). For a finite étale cover the coordinate of C is an étale coordinate of C′ and Frobenius lifts extend uniquely, so the hypotheses hold.
acceptance: For the generic-to-local embedding E_η⊂E_α this is Corollary 3.15; for E⊂E_L it is the growth-zero case of Ohkubo Lemma 7.10.
For the logarithmic rank-two connection over B, the unbounded solution stays unbounded over every B′, while its constant solution stays bounded.

sources.match: Proposition 3.14 proves that the bounded solutions of E_α⊗M_η are the E^τ_α-span of those of M_η, using that a finite-dimensional subspace of the larger complete field carries the product topology; Corollary 3.15 deduces (E_α⊗M_η)^b=E_α⊗M_η^b. The argument uses only an extension of complete valued differential fields sharing the coordinate.
Lemma 7.10 shows the log-growth filtration of a (φ,∇)-module over E commutes with the coefficient extension E_L/E for an isometric extension L/K; at growth zero this is the bounded kernel.

nodes.title: Opposite slope rank bound
nodes.statement: Let (E†,E) be either the parent bounded Robba and Amice fields (residue field k((t))) or D'Addezio's generic pair of §4.2 (residue field k(t)), with k perfect. Let M† be a φ-module over E†, M=E⊗M†, P an isoclinic φ-module over E, and f:M→P a φ-morphism whose restriction to M† is injective. Then λmax(M)=slope(P) and rank_E Top(M)≤rank_E P; if moreover f is surjective (E·f(M†)=P), equality holds. Connections play no role, and f itself need not be injective.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: Extend to the algebraic overconvergent carrier: the multiplication map from the completed tensor product to the algebraic completed field is injective (parent tensor descent), so f|M† stays injective after base change to E†_alg.

The first reverse-filtration piece of M†_alg is pure of the maximal slope of M (Laurent case: the parent reverse filtration over Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}]; k(t) case: D'Addezio Theorem 4.2.6 as corrected in the parent comparison node); its image is a nonzero φ-submodule of the pure P⊗E_alg, so the slopes agree.

After adjoining p^{1/r}, the Frobenius eigenvectors of slope s/r in that first piece span a space of dimension rank Top(M), and they inject into the corresponding eigenspace of P, of dimension rank P; this gives rank Top(M)≤rank P (D'Addezio Lemma 4.2.7; Tsuzuki Theorem 2.13).
If f is surjective it kills the lower slope part of M by Hom vanishing between distinct slopes, so it factors through Top(M) and rank P≤rank Top(M) (Tsuzuki Theorem 2.14).
acceptance: An E†-injection need not stay injective after E-linearisation; the rank conclusion concerns Top(M).

sources.match: Theorem 2.13 shows that an injective Frobenius-compatible map from a φ-module over Ẽ† into Ẽ forces the first opposite slope piece to have slope 0 and dimension 1; Theorem 2.14 deduces that an injective E†-map N†→M into a one-slope M, compatible with Frobenius and generating M, forces the maximal slope of N to equal the slope of M and dim N/N¹=dim M.

Lemma 4.2.7, over D'Addezio's generic carriers with residue field k(t), shows that a φ-morphism M→N to an isoclinic N which is injective on M† forces the maximal slope of M to be that of N and bounds the rank of the top graded piece by rank N, through de Jong's reverse filtration (Theorem 4.2.6).

nodes.title: Frobenius-fixed coefficient normalisation
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero with residue field k of characteristic p and σ a q-Frobenius on K. (1) The fixed field K^σ is complete discretely valued with residue field of at most q elements, hence finite over Q_p. (2) There is a finite unramified extension K′/K to which σ extends such that (K′)^σ has residue field F_q and the same value group as K; if k is perfect, (K′)^σ⊗_{W(F_q)}W(k′)→K′ is an isomorphism with σ=id⊗Frob_q. Consequently every element of |K^×| is |b| for some b∈(K′)^σ, and a rank-one (φ,∇)-module over E, E_η or A†_{C,K} becomes unit-root after the constant twist by b^{-1} over K′.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with residue field k (perfect in the last assertion of (2)) of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: A σ-fixed element a of the valuation ring satisfies a^q≡a modulo the maximal ideal, so the residue field of K^σ embeds in F_q; K^σ is closed in K, hence complete (Tsuzuki Lemma A.1(1), p.37).

Let K̂^{perf,ur} be the p-adic completion of the maximal unramified extension of the completed perfection of K along σ; σ extends uniquely, and its fixed field has residue field F_q and the value group of K. Take K′=(K̂^{perf,ur})^σ·K (Tsuzuki proof of Lemma A.1(2), p.38, reading 'valuation group' for 'valuation ring', E23).

For perfect k compare ramification to identify K′ with (K′)^σ⊗_{W(F_q)}W(k′). A rank-one φ-module has Frobenius eigenvalue of absolute value in |K^×|, so twisting by the constant object with Frobenius b^{-1}, b∈(K′)^σ, gives slope zero.
acceptance: For K=W(F̄_p)[1/p] with the Witt Frobenius, K^σ=Q_p and K′=K.
For K=Q_p(√p) with σ=id (q=p), K^σ=K and the rank-one constant object with Frobenius √p is untwisted by b=√p; the value group, not just |p|^ℤ, is needed.

sources.match: Lemma A.1(1) shows K^σ is a complete discretely valued field with residue field of at most q elements, finite over Q_p; Lemma A.1(2) gives a finite unramified K′/K to which σ extends with (K′)^σ having residue field F_q and the value group of K, and for perfect k identifies K′ with (K′)^σ⊗W(k′).

nodes.title: PBQ filtration
nodes.statement: There is a unique filtration 0=P₀M⊂P₁M⊂⋯⊂P_rM=M whose successive nonzero grades G_i=P_iM/P_(i−1)M are PBQ with strictly decreasing λ_i=λmax(G_i). P₁M is the largest PBQ subobject of maximal slope λmax(M), and subsequent terms are obtained from that construction on the quotient. For M=0 the length is zero.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: First construct a nonzero PBQ subobject of maximal slope: take the preimage in M of the maximal pure summand of B(M). If this preimage is PBQ use it; otherwise it is proper and induction on rank supplies its maximal PBQ subobject (CT11 Proposition 5.4, p.56).

Sum PBQ subobjects of this fixed maximal slope, using the quotient criterion and finite length, to obtain the unique largest one. The next quotient has strictly smaller maximal slope, so induction gives the filtration.
Compare the unique first term and apply induction to the quotient to prove uniqueness.
acceptance: The zero module has the empty sequence of nonzero grades.
A nonzero pure object has one step.
For L_1⊕L_0 of slopes 1 and 0, grades have slopes 1 then 0; the nested second term still has maximal slope 1.

nodes.title: PBQ filtration base change
nodes.statement: For an extension B⊂B′ as in bounded-base-change (in particular E_η⊂E_α, finite coefficient extension, or the finite unramified extension of generic fields of a finite étale cover), M is PBQ iff B′⊗M is PBQ, with the same maximal slope, and B′⊗P_•(M) is the PBQ filtration of B′⊗M. In particular maximal PBQ subobjects and their graded slopes are preserved.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: Bounded-base-change gives B(B′⊗M)=B′⊗B(M); Frobenius slopes of a φ-module are unchanged by field extension, so purity of the bounded quotient is preserved and reflected (Tsuzuki Theorem 3.21(1)).
The base change of the PBQ filtration of M has PBQ grades with strictly decreasing maximal slopes, so by uniqueness of the PBQ filtration over B′ it is the PBQ filtration of B′⊗M (Theorem 3.21(2)).

nodes.title: Bounded-disc PBQ descent
nodes.statement: For a finite free (φ,∇)-module over K[[t]]₀ the PBQ filtration of its E-realisation descends uniquely to saturated differential Frobenius submodules over K[[t]]₀, whose quotient modules are finite free.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: For a bounded-disc M, extend to E†. The de Jong Proposition 6.4 subobject comparison between this module and its bounded Robba extension is the exact RD.1 supplier requested here.

Apply dagger-pbq-descent to get the maximal PBQ submodule over E†, and bring it back through that comparison. Equivalently use CT11 Lemma 5.7 pure-target slope detection in the kernel induction of Theorem 5.6.
Induct on the quotient and use full faithfulness for uniqueness.

nodes.title: Bounded Robba PBQ descent
nodes.statement: For M†/E†, its PBQ filtration over E descends uniquely to E†; equivalently its maximally PBQ subobject descends, and the construction iterates on the quotient. Here k is perfect and the source Frobenius hypotheses of Ohkubo §12.3 are retained.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: If M† is already PBQ there is nothing to descend. Otherwise choose a pure quotient Q of B(M) of slope strictly below λmax(M), using bounded splitting.
Let N†=ker(M†→Q). The image is nonzero and injects into pure Q; opposite-rank-bound identifies its maximal slope with slope Q, so N† is proper and its completion retains the full top quotient of M.

The uniqueness characterisation of the maximal PBQ subobject identifies P₁(N)=P₁(M). Induct on the smaller rank N†, then on the quotient to obtain the full filtration. No arbitrary completed-subobject descent is assumed.
acceptance: For M†/E†, its PBQ filtration over E descends uniquely to E†; equivalently its maximally PBQ subobject descends, and the construction iterates on the quotient. Here k is perfect and the source Frobenius hypotheses of Ohkubo §12.3 are retained.

nodes.title: Logarithmic growth filtration
nodes.statement: For λ≥0, E[[u]]_λ consists of analytic series Σa_nu^n for which there is a real C≥0 with |a_n|≤C(n+1)^λ for all n. For λ<0 set this space to zero. Define Solη,λ(M) by requiring every image of a finite module basis to belong to this space. For bounded-disc solutions use K in place of E. The definition is independent of the finite basis.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. E, E† and K[[t]]₀ are the parent Amice, bounded Robba and bounded-disc carriers. Frobenius is horizontal and invertible after linearisation.
proofSteps: Use a uniform coefficient norm and real powers; multiplication by bounded series preserves the bound by the nonarchimedean convolution estimate.
Define the solution filtration by target growth and compare bases using bounded transition matrices.
acceptance: A nonzero constant has exact growth zero.
log(1+u) has growth at most one, but is not in Fil₀; the subsequence n=p^r witnesses this.
Fil_λ=0 for λ<0, even though a nonzero polynomial has a formal coefficient bound with negative powers after enlarging C.

nodes.title: Dagger sections as generic and local intersections
nodes.statement: In the setting of MS.0/curve-generic-field: (1) Â_{C,K}=⋂_{α∈C}(E_η∩K_α[[x_α]]₀); (2) A†_{C,K}=⋂_{α∈C̄∖C}(E†_α∩Â_{C,K})=⋂_{α∈C}(E_η∩K_α[[x_α]]₀)∩⋂_{α∈C̄∖C}(E_η∩E†_α), the intersections taken in the fields E_α; (3) for a finite projective A†_{C,K}-module M†, M†=⋂_{α∈C}(M_η∩M_{0,α})∩⋂_{α∈C̄∖C}(M_η∩M†_α) inside M_η.

C is affine with a smooth lift and Frobenius lift as in MS.0/curve-generic-field; C̄ is its smooth completion.
proofSteps: All rings in (1) are p-adically complete with the value group of K, so (1) reduces modulo the maximal ideal to k[C]=⋂_{α∈C}(k(C)∩k(α)[[x_α]]), which holds because k[C] is a normal one-dimensional domain (Tsuzuki Lemma 3.2(1), p.12).

For a boundary point α choose an affine open V⊂C̄ containing α in which α is cut out by one function. Lemma 3.1(3) gives the overconvergence-along-α ring as E†_α∩(sections over V∖{α}), by splitting a Laurent series into its negative and nonnegative parts and using Â_V=R[[x_α]]∩Â_C; glue over the finitely many boundary points (Tate acyclicity) to get the first equality of (2); the second follows from (1).
A finite projective module is a direct summand of a finite free module, and the intersections in (2) commute with finite direct sums and summands; this gives (3) (Tsuzuki proof of Lemma 3.33, p.20).
acceptance: On C=G_m with C̄=P¹, the series Σ_{n≥0}p^nx^{p^n} lies in Â_{C,K} and in E_η, but not in E†_∞, so it is not in A†_{C,K}; the boundary condition at ∞ is essential.

nodes.title: Finite étale PBQ transport
nodes.statement: For a finite étale surjective map f:C′→C of smooth connected curves, f* preserves PBQ, and f_* reflects PBQ: if f_*M† is PBQ then M† is PBQ. The source proof is circular (E12); this node proves the pullback assertion directly from the field-extension case of bounded-base-change.
hypotheses: C is a smooth connected curve over perfect k; the coefficient datum is as above. Dagger objects are overconvergent F-isocrystals and their undecorated realisations are convergent. Slopes are normalised by q, so duality negates them and O(1) has slope −1.

nodes.title: Quasi-saturated rank theorem
nodes.statement: A quasi-saturated N†⊂P with P pure is saturated and Top(E⊗N†)→P is an isomorphism. A local dagger object is irreducible iff it is PBQ and saturated and its top quotient is irreducible.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0, q=p^s (s>0), and an isometric lift σ of q-Frobenius. In the last case, total rank two forces splitting.

Apply the PBQ quotient criterion and top-map kernels in each slope order; full faithfulness detects splitting.

nodes.title: Curve graded recovery
nodes.statement: For slope-filtered realisations, a convergent isomorphism B_C(N)→B_C(M) induces a unique dagger isomorphism between the direct sums of the saturated graded PBQ pieces, compatible with the given map on each maximal pure quotient. nodes.title: Dagger hull
nodes.statement: For a convergent sub-F^n-isocrystal N⊂M where M comes from M†, Hull†_M(N) is the smallest convergent subobject of M containing N which extends overconvergently as a subobject of M†. proofSteps: The family is nonempty since it contains M. Choose a member of minimal rank; intersections stay dagger-extendable by exact full faithfulness and cannot lower rank.
Thus it is contained in every member and contains N, independently of the chosen minimal-rank member.

nodes.title: Affine integral models
nodes.statement: For n≥1 let A_n be the image of W(k)⟨u₁,…,u_n⟩→W(k)⟨u⟩, u_i↦pu^i; write ū_i=pu^i. Let B_n be the image in O_E of (A_n[t])_(p,t,ū₁,…,ū_n), where u=1/t. Let B′_n=A_n[t]/(ū₁t−p), and B̃_n its localisation at that ideal. B̃_n→B_n has kernel killed by p^(n−1); colim A_n[1/p]=K⟨u⟩† and colim B̂_n[1/p]=colim B̃̂_n[1/p]=E†.

proofSteps: Use restricted-series generators, ordinary ring images and localisation, then p-adic completion.
The relations ū_it^i=p hold in B_n, while p^(i−1)(ū_it^i−p) follows from ū₁t=p; this gives the stated bounded kernel.
Compare radii of convergence of finitely many generators to identify both filtered colimits.

u is not an integral generator of A₁, while pu is; replacing A_n by W⟨u⟩ changes the induced topology.

nodes.title: Étale affine-line reduction
nodes.statement: For a smooth connected curve C over a perfect field k there is a dense open U⊂C with a finite étale morphism U→A¹_k (Kedlaya). nodes.title: Docile Lefschetz full faithfulness
nodes.statement: Let (X̄,Z) be a smooth connected projective variety over a perfect field k (any base tuple, Abe–Esnault Remark 2.5), dim X̄≥2, with Z a simple normal crossings divisor. Let C̄ be a smooth curve that is a complete intersection of ample divisors in good position with respect to Z (transverse to every stratum of Z); put X=X̄∖Z and C=C̄∩X. Restriction from docile overconvergent isocrystals on X to docile overconvergent isocrystals on C is fully faithful, and so is its Frobenius version. Essential surjectivity is not claimed.
hypotheses: X̄ is smooth connected projective over a perfect field of characteristic p and Z⊂X̄ a simple normal crossings divisor; docile means unipotent monodromy along Z (parent RD.5). The curve C̄ is a complete intersection of ample divisors in good position with respect to Z.
proofSteps: For any two docile objects, internal Hom is docile. Their nilpotent log extensions give the H⁰ restriction isomorphism of AE Corollary 2.4.
Identify horizontal H⁰ with Hom and take the Frobenius-fixed part for F-morphisms.
The supporting localisation/vanishing theorem of AE Theorems 2.2–2.3 belongs to the shared arithmetic D-module continuation and is recorded as gap G3 until that supplier exists.
acceptance: Let (X̄,Z) be as stated, with C̄ a complete intersection of ample divisors in good position with respect to Z. For docile E,F on X, Hom(E,F)→Hom(E|C,F|C) is bijective.

Corollary 2.4 shows that restriction of H⁰ is an isomorphism for tame isocrystals with nilpotent residues along a complete intersection of ample divisors in good position with respect to Z; Remark 2.5 says the argument holds for any base tuple, not only finite fields.

nodes.title: Lefschetz condition

Define LC_Q̄p using irreducibility in the coefficient-extended category. Different objects may require different curves through α.
hypotheses: X is smooth connected over perfect k, α a closed point. Coefficients are fixed K or Q̄_p as explicitly indicated.
proofSteps: Specify the curve, its morphism, the rational lift of α and the irreducible restricted coefficient as the witnessing data.
The condition does not require a closed immersion or a common curve for two objects.

For a rank-one coefficient, every smooth connected curve through α with nonzero pullback witnesses irreducibility.

nodes.title: Overconvergent Q̄_p-F_q-isocrystals
nodes.statement: Let X be of finite type over k=F_q with K=W(k)[1/p] and σ=id. For a finite extension L of K in Q̄_p, an overconvergent L-F_q-isocrystal is an overconvergent F-isocrystal M† on X/K with a K-algebra map L→End(M†); morphisms commute with L. Scalar extension θ_{L₁,L₂}(M†)=M†⊗_{L₁}L₂ satisfies θ_{L₂,L₃}∘θ_{L₁,L₂}≅θ_{L₁,L₃}. The category F_q-Isoc†(X)⊗Q̄_p is the 2-colimit over finite L⊂Q̄_p, with Q̄_p-rank(M†)=rank(M†)/[L:K] on each component; tensor products and duals are taken over L. For k_n/k of degree n with projection π_n:X_n→X there are a pullback π*_{n,Q̄_p}, which identifies the q^n-Frobenius K_n-structure with the coefficient K_n-structure through the chosen embedding K_n⊂L, and a pushforward π_{n,Q̄_p*} right adjoint to it, with Q̄_p-rank(π*_{n,Q̄_p}N†)=Q̄_p-rank(N†) and Q̄_p-rank(π_{n,Q̄_p*}M†)=n·Q̄_p-rank(M†). The Frobenius fibre at a closed point α of degree n is the L-space i*_αM† with the L-linear endomorphism F^n.
hypotheses: X is a separated scheme of finite type over F_q; K=W(F_q)[1/p], σ=id, and an algebraic closure Q̄_p of K is fixed. Coefficients are modelled by a finite L before passing to the 2-colimit; traces and determinants are computed on finite L-models.
proofSteps: Define L-structures and θ_{L₁,L₂} (Tsuzuki Definition 7.1, Example 7.2, Proposition 7.5 with the transitivity index corrected, E16) and take the 2-colimit (Definition 7.6).

Tensor products and duals over L: Propositions 7.3–7.4; the perfect pairing is the K-dual identified with the L-dual through the trace of L/K and the multiplication projector (E17). Irreducible objects are direct sums of copies of an irreducible F-isocrystal over K (Lemma 7.7).

Constant-field pullback and pushforward: §7.2, built from the Appendix B functors π*_{(L,σ^n)/(K,σ)}, π_{(L,σ^n)/(K,σ)*}, their adjunction and trace, with the rank formulas; the overconvergent descent along X_n→X is the parent's étale descent.
Frobenius fibres and their traces at closed points: §7.3, Lemma 7.11, computed on the finite L-model and only then extended to Q̄_p (E18, E26).

θ_{L,L} is the identity and Q̄_p-rank is invariant under θ.
For an object with L-structure, M†⊗_K L with its new L-structure has Q̄_p-rank equal to the K-rank of M†, not rank(M†)/[L:K].

Saturation of the irreducible side and the PBQ quotient criterion give uniqueness.

nodes.title: Projected trace average
nodes.statement: Let k_m/k have degree m>0. On Hom between finite coefficient models of N† and M† after constant extension, let T be conjugation by their q-Frobenius, so T^m=1 on q^m-Frobenius morphisms. Define Av(f)=m⁻¹Σ_{i=0}^{m−1}T^i(f). It is q-Frobenius invariant and descends. In the induction/trace presentation first project K_m⊗_K L≅∏_{j=0}^{m−1}L to the component fixed by the chosen embedding, then the coefficient-projected unit–trace composite is m·id, not m²·id.
hypotheses: X is smooth connected over F_q; coefficients are Q̄_p and q-Frobenius. M† and N† are irreducible and their convergent realisations have slope filtrations. Top denotes the last, maximal-slope quotient.
proofSteps: Choose a finite L containing K_m and all matrix coefficients; split the finite étale coefficient algebra and apply its primitive idempotent before taking the cyclic Frobenius summands.
The projected induction is ⊕_{i=0}^{m−1}F^{i*}N. Its unit sends v to (F^(−i)v)_i and its trace sends (v_i) to ΣF^i(v_i), so the composite has exactly m copies of v.

Use the existing Representation.averageMap for the finite cyclic conjugation representation. Its invariant image and identity-on-invariants laws give descent and preservation of the prescribed quotient map.

For m=2 and T²=1, Av(f)=(f+T(f))/2 is invariant and fixes any T-invariant f.
For L², multiplication by e₁=(1,0) has L-linear trace 1, while multiplication by 1=(1,1) has trace 2; using the latter in each of two induction slots gives 4 rather than 2.

nodes.statement: Let 0→L→M→Q→0 be an exact sequence over E with pure L,Q of slopes a,b. It splits as differential Frobenius modules if b<a, or b−a>1, or M is bounded and 0<b−a≤1.
